title: Jersey City rent-control exemption scope clarification (Ord. 25-099)
requirement: State-law exemptions apply only to the Chapter 260 provisions that directly limit periodic or regular increases in base rentals (260-3(A) and (B)); no dwelling, landlord or owner is exempt from any other administrative, disclosure or registration requirement.
coverage_conditions: All Jersey City dwellings. The exemption clarified applies to newly constructed dwellings built June 25, 1987 through June 25, 1992, not for senior citizens, if the owner complied with state filing and notice requirements.

coverage_quotes: the provisions of this chapter which limit the periodic or regular increases in base rentals of dwelling units shall not apply to a newly constructed dwelling which is constructed between June 25, 1987, through June 25, 1992
no dwelling, landlord, or owner, regardless of rent control status, is exempt from any other provision of Chapter 260.

exemptions: Provisions limiting periodic or regular base-rent increases do not apply to newly constructed dwellings built June 25, 1987 through June 25, 1992, not for senior citizens, for up to the mortgage amortization period or 30 years, whichever is less, if the owner complied with state filing and notice requirements.
penalty: Subsequent compliance is effective only prospectively and does not legalize or validate any rent increase taken during noncompliance.
quoted_span: In accordance with the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Act, N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.2, Jersey City affirms that exemptions granted thereunder apply only to those provisions of Chapter 260 which directly limit the periodic or regular increases in base rentals, and do not extend to any other administrative, disclosure, or registration requirement of Chapter 260.
interaction: Municipal section operates within the limitations imposed by the New Jersey Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Act.
